source.title: New trends and open problems in fuzzy logic and approximate reasoning

trace.notes: Input normalized as a zbMATH bibliographic resolver URL with trailing identifier 1265034. Local shard metadata and independent resolver metadata identify the work as Didier Dubois and Henri Prade, New trends and open problems in fuzzy logic and approximate reasoning, Theoria 11(3), pages 109-121, 1996; the corresponding Zbl identifier found during resolver recovery is Zbl 0922.03035.

failure_mode=blocked_or_challenged; secondary_failure_modes=network_or_dns_failure, metadata_only. Local shell fetch of https://zbmath.org/1265034 failed because outbound DNS resolution is unavailable in the sandbox. Browser/search recovery found only zbMATH serial metadata, PhilPapers metadata/abstract, and HAL CV metadata for hal-04039817v1, none of which is a readable primary source containing the problem statements.

Identifier-specific recovery used the zbMATH id 1265034, Zbl 0922.03035, exact title searches, the PhilPapers record DUBNTA-7, the PDC links exposed by PhilPapers, the HAL record hal-04039817v1, and the Theoria OJS archive. The HAL document endpoint returned an access-denied challenge. The OJS archive states that Theoria provides free access from 2003 onward and directs earlier archive access to PDC/POIESIS and JSTOR; the target 1996 issue was not recovered as readable full text through the OJS pages.

Bounded exact-work search attempts included the exact title, the exact title plus PDF, the exact title plus PDC, hal-04039817, Zbl 0922.03035, and the Theoria issue metadata. No candidate page or file was accepted because remaining accessible results were metadata records, abstracts, archive indexes, subscription or blocked pages, or unrelated fuzzy-logic works.

No accepted questions were produced because no readable exact-work PDF or full HTML source containing the article conclusion and problem statements was recovered. Extracting from zbMATH metadata, PhilPapers abstracts, HAL metadata, OJS archive listings, search snippets, or related papers would violate the source adequacy, evidence coverage, and no-new-facts gates.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/1265034.json and outputs/latest.json.
